artificial intelligence is moving
to the core of financial
services organizations.
it is shaping decisions in real time and
influencing outcomes at scale. as that happens,
technology alone is no longer the differentiator.
structure, ownership and operating rhythm
become just as important as capability.
through this research, we set out to understand
how institutions are responding to this shift.
what we found is a sector that recognizes the
opportunity yet is still recalibrating the way it
works. many organizations have invested heavily
in platforms and tools. fewer have redesigned
the system that connects insight to action.
the next phase of transformation will be defined
less by deployment and more by alignment.
alignment between business and technology.
alignment between data and decision rights.
alignment between ambition and execution.
the institutions that succeed will be those that
create clarity around ownership, empower
teams to act within defined guardrails and build
modern data platforms that allow innovation to
scale without increasing risk.
rewiring for the future is about building
adaptability into the core of the organization. it is
about ensuring intelligence is trusted, actionable
and sustainable.
the opportunity ahead is significant. so is the
responsibility. i hope the insights in this report help
leaders reflect not only on what they are building,
but on how they are organizing to build it.

rewiring financial services
ai is no longer a competitive advantage in
financial services. it is a structural stress test. it
is exposing whether institutions are designed
to turn intelligence into meaningful, trusted
experiences at scale.
across the sector, the journey from ai pilot to
scaled implementation is compressing rapidly.
what was experimental just two years ago is now
moving into production environments at pace.
our research shows that 77% of ai initiatives are
progressing from pilot to production — clear
evidence that technological capability has
outpaced the operating structures designed to
govern it.
the constraint is no longer model performance
or infrastructure maturity. it sits in how
organizations work: how decisions are made, how
data is owned and how intelligence is connected
to action.
as firms push initiatives beyond post-pilot
into scaled delivery, standard team structures,
centralized decision flows and fragmented data
ownership are becoming sources of friction rather
than enablers of value.
this is not for lack of effort. banks, insurers and
wealth managers have spent more than a decade
digitizing services layered on top of legacy estates.
generative ai now offers a genuine opportunity to
leapfrog a generation of accumulated tech debt.
but friction remains in ownership, governance and
the way teams come together around outcomes.
